titles.title: Thief2
titles.engine: Dark Engine with NewDark 1.26. Thief2.exe ProductVersion 1.26, md5 1109955d4d0a7855592b33d954abcb76, PE subsystem 5.0, imports MSVCR90/MSVCP90; D3DX9_43 is in the tree. The staged cam_ext.cfg turns on use_d3d_display, single_display_mode 2, ui_scale_mode 2, force_32bit and force_32bit_textures, so the game runs NewDark's Direct3D 9 display at 32 bpp.
titles.launch_sets: 1920x1080x32, fullscreen D3D9, measured live on .145 on 2026-09-29 at 00:42 through the staged 'Play Thief 2.bat'. Thief2.log reads 'game_screen_size 1920 1080', 'D3DProvider StartMode: smode 1920x1080x32' and 'CreateDevice: res = D3D_OK ; 1920x1080 ... fs=1', and the Video page shows 'Resolution: 1920x1080x32'. The mechanism works as claimed. The launcher runs FLEETRES.EXE -setline cam.cfg game_screen_size %FR_W% %FR_H%; -setline joins its arguments and appends the line if it is missing. The staged FLEETRES.EXE md5 bb180f3b... matches the repo build, and stage-fleetres.py --check at origin/master reports '0 staged, 216 already current, 0 failures'. GAMESYNC writes the same line through the gameres.h:764 GR_OP_SETLINE rule, so both writers produce 'game_screen_size 1920 1080' on these panels. The deployed cam.cfg on .123, .145, .195 and .240 is byte-identical to the staged file with only that line changed (md5 62c80448...). .145, .195 and .240 still carry the 1658-byte launcher (dated 2026-09-28 17:08Z); .123 carries the current 2012-byte one. Both versions contain the FLEETRES line.
titles.menu_source: Seen on hardware on .145 (XP, GeForce 8400GS). Options -> Video -> 'Resolution:' opens a list with 12 visible rows and scroll arrows: 640x480x32, 720x480x32, 720x576x32, 800x600x32, 1024x768x32, 1152x864x32, 1280x720x32 / 16:9, 1280x768x32 / 15:9, 1280x800x32 / 16:10, 1280x960x32, 1280x1024x32, 1360x768x32 / 16:9, 1600x900x32 / 16:9, 1680x1050x32 / 16:10, 1920x1080x32 / 16:9. The last entry is 1920x1080x32 / 16:9. The code matches the earlier reading. The builder at 0x45236b uses the 3D device's list of mode ids, keeps depth {16,32} (only 32 with force_32bit), w >= 400 and 300 <= h <= 4800, and stops at 64 accepted entries (cmp [edi+0x12c6],0x40 at 0x4524f4). The candidates come from the hardcoded 159-entry grd table at 0x786768, which has 1920x1080x16 (id 105) and 1920x1080x32 (id 141), flag byte 0x81. The 'current mode has flag 0x20' filter never applies, because no table entry carries 0x20. Driver modes missing from the table are dropped, for example 1600x1024 on .145 and 1152x648/1776x1000 on .195. The Thief2.log mode lists show 1920x1080x32 accepted on all four LCD boxes.

titles.fix: None needed for the menu or the launch. Optional housekeeping, not resolution-related: GAMESYNC .145, .195 and .240 so they get the current 2012-byte launcher.
titles.fix_risk: No change proposed. Things to know: (1) Leaving Options through Done makes NewDark rewrite cam.cfg (game_screen_depth 32, game_screen_flags 45, fogging 1, sfx_channels 48, skip_intro, reverse_stereo 0) and create user.bnd. A resolution picked in the menu therefore lands in cam.cfg, and FLEETRES and GAMERES overwrite it at the next launch or sync. The menu offers 1080p, but a different choice does not persist. That is by design. (2) GAMESYNC re-copies the staged cam.cfg (1379 B, 800 600) on every sync because the deployed file differs in size and time, and GAMERES then rewrites it. A settled box therefore never reports 0 files written and 0 values changed. The fix for this is on branch fix-gameres-sync-fight (commit 64baa19, a per-box ledger of GAMERES edits); it is not on master. (3) .240's EDID was present again at 00:54; with no EDID, both writers fall back to the 4:3 branch.
titles.hw_check: On an idle XP LCD box (WINLIST first): EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Thief2" "Play Thief 2.bat", wait 25 s, then SCREENSHOT 0 (XP GDI captures the D3D9 surface). NewDark's cursor is not 1:1 with the Windows cursor: in-game x = 240 + 0.75 * UICLICK x, while y is unchanged. To click something drawn at screen X, send UICLICK (X-240)/0.75. Measured sequence on .145: Options = UICLICK 956 742, Video tab = 946 98, 'Resolution:' = 956 488, list down arrow (drawn at 1538,960) = UICLICK 1731 960, three clicks, then the last row reads '1920x1080x32 / 16:9'. Do not click near the rows. The row hit area spans the whole panel, and an off-text click at 1400,700 selected 1280x720. Leave with Back = 960 378, Done = 1203 206, Quit = 1189 948, and require DISPLAYCFG get = 1920x1080 afterwards. Then restore cam.cfg to its pre-test bytes and delete user.bnd, or accept that the next launch or sync rewrites them. On .195 (Win7) use Thief2.log and WINLIST.
titles.verifier_notes: CONFIRMED, and upgraded from inferred to observed: the fullscreen 1920x1080x32 list containing 1920x1080 was photographed on .145. Corrections: (a) the hw_check's 'UICLICK works' holds only near screen centre; the cursor is scaled, x_game = 240 + 0.75*x_os. (b) Leaving Options through Done writes cam.cfg and user.bnd. My test did this on .145; I restored cam.cfg byte-for-byte (md5 62c80448...) and deleted user.bnd. Thief2.log on .145 now holds my run. (c) Added the sync-churn note. Nothing else refuted.

titles.title: ThiefGold
titles.engine: Dark Engine, vanilla, no NewDark. THIEF.EXE ProductVersion 1.37, md5 8dd515df75176bcd1caaf65a93f47d81, PE subsystem 4.0, sections .text/lgalloc/.rdata/.data/.rsrc, no stxt section. There is no NewDark runtime in the tree: no D3DX9_43, MSVCR90 or cam_ext.cfg.
titles.launch_sets: 640x480, confirmed. 'Play Thief Gold.bat' only does cd /d plus start "" thief.exe. There is no FLEETRES, no gameres.h rule, and no game_screen_size in CAM.CFG, USER.CFG, DARK.CFG or install.cfg. Deployed CAM.CFG on .123, .145, .195 and .240 has md5 68f695ec..., identical to staged. The default ScrnMode (0x4108d0 -> 0x5e1a40) is {7, 640, 480, depth 8, screen_flags 13}; flags 13 includes hardware bit 0x4. The reader at 0x43b190 overrides it from game_screen_size, game_screen_depth, game_screen_flags, game_full_screen and game_hardware. The 08-31 compat 'verified 640x480' rows are intro-movie frames. I viewed the .123 and .246 frames ('LEST YE BE STRUCK DOWN'); they say nothing about the Video list.
titles.menu_source: Hardcoded table. The only mode table the engine can use is grd_mode_info at 0x615f44: 87 entries with w/h/bpp at +0/+2/+4, maximum 1600x1200, 4:3/5:4 plus 640x400/320x200 only, no 16:9 or 16:10 entry. The lookup at 0x535be0 scans 0x57 entries and returns -1 otherwise, so 1920x1080, 1280x960 and 1152x864 cannot be named even from a cfg. The Options -> Video builder at 0x51cfd0 takes the hardware branch only when a D3D driver exists and screen_flags bit 4 is set. That branch lists the 3D device's modes with bpp == 16, w >= 400 and 300 <= h <= 768. The software branch lists the static ids at 0x611df0 (400x300x8, 512x384x8, 640x400x8, 640x480x8, 800x600x8). The list shows 12 rows per page with a scroll offset at [ebx+0x12cc]; this is a page size, not a hard total. Menu ceiling: 1024x768x16 (hardware) or 800x600x8 (software).

titles.fix: REFUTES the claim that 'without new files nothing reaches 1080p'. The NewDark package already staged in Thief2 documents a Thief 1 mode. new_config_vars.txt (1.26) says: 'dark1 - added to cam.cfg to tell game to run in Thief1 mode. It also requires a couple of extra patch resources to make the menu system fully usable.' The staged Thief2.exe 1.26 contains the string 'dark1', and Thief2/doc/T1.7z holds those resources (INTRFACE.CRF plus a readme). Route A, no download: build a ThiefGold tree in the XP build VM that runs the XP-proven Thief2.exe 1.26 on the TG data. Add dark1 to cam.cfg or cam_ext.cfg. Add the T1 INTRFACE.CRF through cam_mod.ini mod_path or a patch directory. Copy msvcr90.dll, msvcp90.dll, Microsoft.VC90.CRT.manifest, D3DX9_43.dll and lgvid.dll from Thief2. Use Thief2's cam_ext.cfg (use_d3d_display, force_32bit, single_display_mode 2, ui_scale_mode 2). Then add the FLEETRES -setline cam.cfg game_screen_size line, the vcr-kmd DX6 swap block through stage-fleetres.py, and the mirrored gameres.h rule, and prove it in the build VM and on metal. Route B, download: the dedicated T1 NewDark engine (TFix engine component). Prefer the 1.26 generation that matches the proven Thief 2 build, and check PE subsystem and imports before staging. Vanilla stopgap, 4:3 only: game_screen_size 1024 768 plus game_screen_depth 16. That is the largest table mode that is also in these drivers' lists, and 1280x960 is not in the table.
titles.fix_source: Route A: already on the share, in /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games-Library/Thief2/ (Thief2.exe 1.26, doc/T1.7z, the VC90 runtime and manifest, D3DX9_43.dll, lgvid.dll, cam_ext.cfg). Route B: would need downloading TFix 1.27d (moddb) or T1 NewDark (ttlg); not on the share (case-insensitive search for thief/newdark/tfix).
titles.fix_risk: Route A: the package's own readme warns 'at heart you're still running Thief 2 ... not 100% authentic and it's not flawless', with occasional AI pathfinding problems that are fixable only by rebuilding a mission's pathfinding database in DromEd. It has not been tried on this data, so a build-VM install and a mission smoke test are required before staging. The exe becomes Thief2.exe, so launch.txt's target changes; keep the TG icon through the icon column. Other risks, shared with Route B: 1.37 saves do not load. NewDark needs Windows 2000 or later and the VC2008 runtime, so .243 (Win98) could never run it; it is already gated there by disk. .124 needs the vcr-kmd DX6 swap. GAMESYNC never deletes, so vanilla files linger. A new SETLINE rule gets the same sync churn as Thief2 until branch fix-gameres-sync-fight lands. Route B: whether 1.27 runs on XP is unverified; the staged 1.26 proves only 1.26. Vanilla stopgap: stays 4:3 and depends on the default hardware flag.

titles.title: SystemShock2
titles.engine: Dark Engine, vanilla retail 1.0. shock2.exe is the SafeDisc 1.11.000 v1 loader (discprotect.py agrees; ProductVersion 1.15; sections .txt/.text/.txt2). SHOCK2.ICD (md5 9ba459f0...) is the encrypted engine. New finding: a decrypted copy of the same retail engine is on the share. /mnt/retro-share/Files/Games/Windows XP/System_Shock_2.zip (and the byte-identical Multiplayer/System_Shock_2.zip, 512,266,038 B) holds SYSTEMSHOCK2.bin (2014, MODE2/2352). Its /CRACK/SHOCK2.EXE is 2,881,536 B, md5 ce16f131..., PE timestamp 1999-07-16, entry point in .text. The same image's SHOCK\ loader and ICD are byte-identical to the staged ones. I used it read-only for analysis only.
titles.launch_sets: When it runs: 640x480x16 hardware. Nothing sets a mode: the generated mount launcher has fleetres_block '' (provisioning/discmount/specs/SystemShock2.json), there is no gameres.h rule, and cam.cfg has no game_screen_size (md5 fc1bf665..., identical on .123, .145, .195 and .240). shock.cfg sets game_screen_depth 16, screen_size 640,480 and hardware 1. The retail default ScrnMode at 0x65ab38 is 640x480. Reaching the game is less settled than the earlier agent says. The 08-31 compat rows 'verified d3d 1920x1080' for .240 and .246 are false: I viewed both frames. .240 shows DAEMON Tools 'Unable to mount image. Cue sheet: Unit is locked.' over the desktop. .246 (now .195) shows 'Cannot locate the CD-ROM' over the Xerxes 'VERIFYING SYSTEMS ACCESS' splash. .145 has the 08-30 WER-crash note in install.reg. The .123 claim is stale: HWPROFILE now reports disc_mount=true (evidence d347bus), C:\Program Files\D-Tools exists, and 'System Shock 2.lnk' is on its desktop. The 08-31 mount-error.txt predates that. No LCD box has been retested since 08-31. I did not launch it, because a SafeDisc run can leave a DAEMON Tools unit locked until reboot (spec note).
titles.menu_source: Hardcoded table, now verified against the retail engine itself rather than inferred from the demo. The decrypted retail SHOCK2.EXE has grd_mode_info at 0x6a973c: 87 entries, maximum 1600x1200, no 16:9 or 16:10 entry, no 1920x1080. The Options -> Video builder at 0x5632c0 takes the 3D device's mode list at bpp == 16 when D3D is present and screen_flags bit 4 is set; otherwise it uses the static list at 0x69d240 (400x300x8, 512x384x8, 640x400x8, 640x480x8, 800x600x8) at bpp == 8. Filter: w >= 640 (0x280), 480 <= h <= 768 (0x1e0..0x300), 12 rows per page. The menu can therefore offer only 640x480, 800x600 and 1024x768. The config reader at 0x43c070 (prefix 'game_') honours game_screen_size, but only for modes in the 87-entry table.

titles.fix: Confirmed: SS2 NewDark (SS2Tool, or the bare package) is the only route to a 1080p menu. The staged Thief 2 NewDark cannot help, because its dark1 mode is Thief-only. Then: (1) drop disc_mount from requires.json; (2) regenerate the launcher from its spec as a plain launcher carrying the FLEETRES -setline cam.cfg game_screen_size line and the vcr-kmd DX6 block; (3) add the mirrored gameres.h rule; (4) add a cam_ext.cfg with use_d3d_display, force_32bit, single_display_mode 2 and ui_scale_mode 2. Prefer the SS2 NewDark build from the same generation as the XP-proven Thief 2 1.26, and check its PE subsystem and imports. Vanilla stopgap: game_screen_size 1024 768 plus game_screen_depth 16. That is 4:3 and still disc-bound.
titles.fix_source: Would need downloading SS2Tool v6.x (systemshock.org topic 4141) or the NewDark 2.4x SS2 package; neither is on the share (case-insensitive search). SS2Tool needs Vista or later, so run it under Wine on the host or in a Win7+ VM against a copy of the staged tree, then capture from there. For the record, the share does hold a decrypted no-CD 1.0 engine (the CRACK folder above). It is not a 1080p fix, having the same 87-entry table, and it conflicts with READ-ME-FIRST's 'nothing here defeats the copy protection', so I do not recommend it.
titles.fix_risk: As before: 1.0 saves are incompatible, the software renderer is dropped, and co-op multiplayer needs every box on the same build. Also: a bare NewDark package may need the official 2.3 data changes that SS2Tool applies, which is untested. SS2Tool's optional mods (SCP and others) must be deselected to stay vanilla. .124 needs the DX6 swap. SHOCK2.ICD and the 650 MB _disc stay on boxes because GAMESYNC never deletes. A new SETLINE rule churns on every sync until branch fix-gameres-sync-fight lands. Launch-testing the current disc build can leave a DAEMON Tools unit locked until reboot, which breaks every other mount launcher on that box.

titles.title: JediKnightDF2
titles.engine: Sith engine. JK.EXE 1.01 (md5 85f8f883bbb7a167429879c899be1803) from the GOG tree with the ogg winmm.dll wrapper. DirectDraw with a DX5 Direct3D HAL path; the GUI and software renderer are 8-bit. It keeps its settings under HKLM (root 0x80000002 at 0x4011fa) in 'Software\LucasArts Entertainment Company\JediKnight\v1.0'. The XP sysmain.sdb entry for JK.EXE, which adds the EmulateCDFS and EmulateGetCommandLine shims, only matches when Jedi.EXE sits beside it. The staged tree has no Jedi.EXE, so no shims apply, and neither shim would touch display modes anyway.
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 8-bpp software on all four LCD boxes, confirmed statically. With no displayMode stored, 0x4146b3 calls FindClosestMode(640x480, 8 bpp), and b3DAccel defaults to off. REGREAD shows only CD Path, InstallType and Version on all four boxes. Correction: these values are not written only when Setup -> Display is closed with OK. They are saved on every clean exit: routine 0x414be0 writes displayDeviceGUID, 3DDeviceGUID, displayMode, b3DAccel and minTextureDimension, and its only caller is the program shutdown sequence (call at 0x4013c5). The boxes have no values because JK has only ever been force-killed there. .195 has UAC off (EnableLUA=0), so HKLM writes land in HKLM; VirtualStore is not involved.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver, with a 64-slot cap. The earlier agent called .240 unknown; I measured it, and it fails there. Sequence at 0x425b60: SetCooperativeLevel 0x51 (ALLOWMODEX|EXCLUSIVE|FULLSCREEN, not DDSCL_NORMAL), then EnumDisplayModes with callback 0x426030, which keeps only 320-wide modes and tags them [ModeX]. Then SetCooperativeLevel 0x11 and EnumDisplayModes with callback 0x425e30, which keeps every mode. One counter covers both passes and they stop at 0x40. The array is copied into the device record unfiltered (0x4277e6). Setup -> Display 'Video Modes' (0x4150c0) filters only by bpp: 16 with 3D Acceleration ticked, 8 without. I reproduced that exact sequence on each box with ddenum.exe (source in evidence). .123: 47 modes, 1920x1080x16 at index 45, listed. .145: 50 modes, index 34, listed. .195 (Win7): 60 modes, index 58, listed with 4 slots spare. .240 (X800): 78 modes (6 from the 320-wide pass plus 72), and 1920x1080x16 is at index 76, past the cap. On .240 the list stops at 1280x1024 (index 61). The ATI XP and Win7 AMD drivers enumerate resolution-major, and .240's driver adds 320x200, 320x240, 400x300, 512x384, 640x400 and 640x432, which is what pushes 1080p past 64. With 3D unticked the same list offers '1920x1080 8bpp' (software) on the three boxes where it fits.

titles.fix: .123, .145 and .195: each box needs displayMode = its own index of 1920x1080x16, plus b3DAccel=1 and the device GUIDs, in HKLM. Route 1, once per box: Setup -> Display, tick 3D Acceleration, pick 1920x1080 16bpp, OK, then Quit from the main menu. JK writes the values at clean exit; a taskkill discards them. Route 2: a launcher-time helper that repeats the enumeration (ddenum.c already does) and writes the values before each launch. The index moves whenever the driver's mode list changes, so it must be recomputed every time; it also differs between DF2 (0x51 pass) and MotS (0x11 pass), for example 45 versus 43 on .123. It must write 3DDeviceGUID too, because the loader drops to defaults when the GUID reads fail. .240: no registry value can reach 1080p, because the mode is never stored. Options, both unverified: make that box's driver enumerate fewer modes before 1080p (13 or more fewer), or binary-patch the JK.EXE/JKM.EXE enumeration callbacks (code cave) to skip 24/32-bpp modes, which the list builder never shows anyway. That leaves 6 + 48 entries on .240, and 1080p fits.
titles.fix_source: .123/.145/.195: already in tree. The engine offers the mode; the helper for Route 2 would be new repo code (ddenum.c is a starting point). .240: nothing on the share. It needs a per-box driver change or an exe patch built in the repo.
titles.fix_risk: The index is per box and per driver list; a stale index selects the wrong mode after a card, driver or monitor change. A clean Quit rewrites HKLM, which the fix wants and a verification pass does not. A force-killed JK or MotS leaves an XP desktop at 640x480 live; I measured this twice and restored it with ChangeDisplaySettings(NULL,0) (regmode.c). 16-bit D3D at 1920x1080 has never been run on these cards, and the Sith renderer is 4:3, so check for stretching. On .195, whether the Win7 legacy D3D HAL enables the 3D checkbox is unverified; without it only 8bpp modes list, 1920x1080 8bpp included. An exe patch changes the md5 on every box. DirectPlay LAN play is unaffected.
titles.hw_check: DF2's 8-bit GUI photographs with wrong colours but intact geometry (the .133 compat note). Two options: run MotS as the GUI proxy, since it runs the same enumeration code; or run the probe, uploading ddenum.exe to C:\RETRO_AGENT, running EXEC "...ddprobe_tmp.exe" x (it prints 'SUMMARY ... 1920x1080x16_index=N LISTED/CUT'), then DELETE it. For DF2 itself: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\JediKnightDF2" JK.EXE, Esc, Setup -> Display -> 3D Acceleration -> scroll 'Video Modes' to the end. The last 16bpp row must be 1920x1080. Leave with Cancel, then taskkill (not Quit, which writes HKLM). Then restore the desktop with ChangeDisplaySettings(NULL,0) and confirm DISPLAYCFG get = 1920x1080 with an unchanged REGREAD of the JK key.
titles.verifier_notes: REFUTED as 'yes': true on 3 of 4 LCD boxes; .240 measured NO (1920x1080x16 enumerated at index 76 of 78, JK keeps 64). Corrections: the first pass uses coop 0x51, not DDSCL_NORMAL. Settings are saved at clean exit, not only on OK. .195 has UAC off, so the VirtualStore caveat does not apply. The earlier count estimate was close on .123, .145 and .195 but ignored the per-box ModeX-pass entries. PER-TITLE-STATUS.md's 'incapable' is still wrong for .123, .145 and .195. A DF2 GUI list was not photographed; the MotS GUI (same code) matched the probe exactly on .240 and .145.

titles.title: JediKnightMotS
titles.engine: Sith engine. JKM.EXE (md5 192d2be2bfbe5a1acc9f562657a7d9ea, no version resource, extra '..idata' section). Same DirectDraw/D3D code as DF2; 16-bit GUI. Settings live in HKLM\Software\LucasArts Entertainment Company LLC\Mysteries of the Sith\v1.0. The XP AppCompat entry needs SITH.EXE beside the exe, which is absent, so no shims apply.
titles.launch_sets: 640x480 at every start on all four LCD boxes, confirmed: the GUI came up at 640x480 on .145 and .240, and no displayMode or b3DAccel is stored. The save routine 0x417560 writes displayDeviceGUID, 3DDeviceGUID, displayMode and b3DAccel, and its only caller is the shutdown sequence (0x4013d5), so the values appear only after a clean Quit. There is no FLEETRES and no gameres rule.
titles.menu_source: Driver list with a 64-slot cap, as in DF2 except that both passes use coop 0x11 (0x428cc7/0x428d05). Callbacks 0x429160 (320-wide only) and 0x428f60 (all), counter [0x5b6bac], cap 0x40. The Setup -> Display 'Available Video Modes' list filters only by bpp. Seen on hardware: on .240 with 'Enable 3D Acceleration' ticked, the list ends at '1280x1024 16bpp'; there is no 1360x768, 1440x900, 1776x1000 or 1920x1080. That is exactly what the probe predicts (index 76 dropped by the 64 cap). On .145 the same list ends '... 1600x900, 1600x1024, 1680x1050, 1920x1080 16bpp'. Probe predictions for the other boxes: .123 and .195 listed (see DF2; .123 index 43 for MotS, which has no ALLOWMODEX pass).

titles.fix: Same as DF2. .123, .145 and .195 need a per-box displayMode index, b3DAccel=1 and the GUIDs. Either set them through Setup -> Display -> tick 3D -> 1920x1080 16bpp -> OK and then a clean Quit, or write them from a launcher helper that repeats MotS's enumeration (coop 0x11 both passes) and recomputes the index every launch. .240 cannot list or store 1080p. It needs a smaller driver mode list or a JKM.EXE callback patch that skips 24/32-bpp modes, both unverified.
titles.fix_source: .123/.145/.195: already in tree (the engine offers the mode). Helper = new repo code. .240: nothing on the share.
titles.fix_risk: Same as DF2: per-box, per-driver index; a clean exit writes HKLM; taskkill leaves XP at 640x480 until ChangeDisplaySettings(NULL,0); 16-bit D3D at 1080p is untested; 3D availability on Win7 .195 is unverified; DirectPlay LAN play is unaffected.
titles.hw_check: Check that no other game window is open (WINLIST), then EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\JediKnightMotS" JKM.EXE, wait 10 s, UIKEY ESCAPE. On the Players screen: Ok = UICLICK 558 449. Main menu: Setup = 544 409. Setup: Display = 318 99. Enable 3D Acceleration = 78 169. List down arrow = 160 381, click about 20 times. The last row must read '1920x1080 16bpp'. The GUI is 640x480x16 and XP SCREENSHOT captures it. Leave with Cancel = 99 449, then EXEC taskkill /f /im "JKM.EXE". A Quit would write displayMode/b3DAccel to HKLM. Then restore the live desktop with ChangeDisplaySettings(NULL,0) (regmode.c, uploaded and deleted) and require DISPLAYCFG get = 1920x1080 plus an unchanged REGREAD of the MotS key. On .195 (Win7) the GUI is exclusive fullscreen and cannot be photographed; use the probe.
titles.verifier_notes: REFUTED as 'yes': seen on hardware, .240's list stops at 1280x1024 16bpp, while .145's reaches 1920x1080 16bpp. Corrections: both enumeration passes use coop 0x11; settings are saved at clean exit, not only on OK; .195 UAC is off. Collision disclosure: my first MotS launch on .145 at about 00:48:30 started while another reviewer's Red Alert 2 window was up (it showed in WINLIST at launch; rts2d-review's last RA2 frame is 00:48:21), and RA2 was gone about 20 s later. My launch may have ended that test; that reviewer's RA2 evidence from about 00:48 on .145 should be treated as suspect. Every run of mine then restored the desktop to 1920x1080x32@60 with the persisted mode untouched, and every temporary helper was deleted and checked by DIRLIST. No MotS files or registry values changed. .240's retro_chat console moved after the mode switch, which is cosmetic.
